primary_source.author: Xuefeng Zhu
primary_source.title: Weil positivity in compact windows: a finite reduction, certified two-sided bounds, and a Landau-Widom decay law

window.selection_reason: first clean rational window above the prime-5 activation threshold (log 5)/2 and above the current full-window certified frontier L=0.8

target_statement: For every complex f in L^2(R) supported in [-161/200,161/200], the exact Riemann-Weil quadratic form Q in the normalization of arXiv:2608.24827v2 is non-negative. The geometric side must retain the pole term, the full archimedean term, every prime-power term with log n < 161/100, and the exact even/odd parity contract.

normalization.fourier_transform: F(t) = integral_R f(u) exp(i t u) du
normalization.weil_symbol: Psi_L(t) = Re psi(1/4 + i t/2) - log pi - sum_{log n < 2L} (2 Lambda(n)/sqrt(n)) cos(t log n)
normalization.even_geometric_form: Q(f) = 2 F(i/2)^2 + (1/(2 pi)) integral_R |F(t)|^2 Psi_L(t) dt for real even f
normalization.complex_contract: decompose real/imaginary and even/odd sectors exactly as in the primary source; the odd pole term has the source-prescribed sign reversal

first_bridge.statement: At L=161/200 the active prime powers are exactly {2,3,4,5}; A_L = sqrt(2) log 2 + (2/sqrt(3)) log 3 + log 2 + (2/sqrt(5)) log 5; and with Tsharp=600 the one-stroke parameter beta* = log(Tsharp/(2 pi)) - 1/Tsharp - A_L satisfies beta* > 97217/600000 > 0. Therefore the hypotheses of the imported one-stroke reduction are met and the even-sector target reduces to the explicit finite leading matrix plus the source-defined tail and coupling bounds.

proof_obligations.description: Lock exact source normalization and prime-comb membership at L=161/200
Assemble the Tsharp=600 even Legendre leading block with certified quadrature and exact n=5 prime term
Prove a positive lower bound for the even leading block and close tail deviation and leading-tail coupling
Repeat the certified reduction in the odd sector with the source-prescribed pole sign
Compose real/imaginary and parity sectors to obtain the complex fixed-window theorem
Independent specialist/certificate replay through MATHCERT if P005 closes

smallest_target_falsifier: A rigorously evaluated admissible test function supported in [-161/200,161/200] with Q(f)<0. A negative eigenvalue of an uncertified truncation or float64 matrix does not qualify.
method_falsifier: Failure of the certified Tsharp=600 leading-block/tail inequality terminates this one-stroke certificate instance but does not by itself falsify RH-R030.
false_proof_fixtures: omitting the newly active n=5 term
using a prime-comb bound in the wrong inequality direction
finite-subspace positivity without a certified tail/coupling bound
float64 eigenvalue signs near the spectral floor
even-sector positivity promoted to arbitrary complex tests without the odd-sector contract
fixed-window positivity promoted to all supports or to RH
non_implications: does not prove RH or RH-T-000
does not prove positivity for any support larger than 161/200
does not certify a new zero range, zero-free region, density estimate, or critical-line proportion
does not establish novelty, priority, or publication readiness
does not validate the retracted L=1.19 certificate
does not create a Hilbert-Pólya operator
certification_route_if_successful: Prepare a new bounded MATHCERT handoff for RH-R030-WEIL-P5-001 containing the exact claim, source identity, certified arithmetic/matrix artifacts, imported-theorem boundary, proof-obligation lineage, and explicit statement that RH-T-000 remains open.
